newsitem.title: USA: Wichita council defers $10 mln hotel rev bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Wichita council defers $10 mln hotel rev bond plan.

text.p: Wichita City Council deferred action Tuesday on the sale of a decades-old hotel downtown and issuance of the last of $10 million of industrial revenue bonds for its renovation at the request of the applicant, a spokesman said.
The owners of Annapolis, Maryland-based Grand Heritage Hotels plan to sell the Broadview hotel downtown along with other properties to Patriot American Hospitality Inc of Dallas.
Grand Heritage would operate the facility, but the transaction requires certain consents and waivers from Wichita.

The City Council approved the overall issuance in January 1996 and $6.4 million of industrial revenue bonds have been issued for the first phase of the reconstruction, said Mike Taylor, spokesman for the city manager's office.
The sale of the hotel to Patriot American will lead to the issuance of the remaining debt and insure that the second phase improvements will qualify for property tax abatement, city documents state.
